transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samir Khan (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Stonemill CISO), Evan Ruiz (Lead DevOps), Priya Varma (Head of ML), Tom Beck (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick intake focused on Stonemill's security gating for adopting Redwood. Main themes: SOC2/ISO requirements, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC and least privilege, audit log fields & retention, encryption and KMS/hardware security module options, and deployment preference between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer leaning toward Redwood Dedicated for predictability but wants to validate KMS and audit capabilities; open to Private if encryption and network isolation requirements can't be met in Dedicated.

Topics covered: SOC2/ISO scope, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC/roles and API key governance, audit logs schema + retention policy, encryption at rest/transport, bring-your-own-key (BYOK) / external KMS, private VPC peering / on-prem gateway, pilot and benchmark criteria.

Transcript body: (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect in places)
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. Quick intros, we'll mostly focus on security gating and hosting options.
[00:08] Maya: Hi, Maya here, CISO at Stonemill. We'll be the ones signing off for production. I have Evan and Priya from infra and ML. Tom is here for procurement notes.
[00:16] Samir: Great, Samir from Redwood AE and with me is Lena, SE.
[00:20] Lena: Hi all. We'll go through how Redwood surfaces audit logs, SSO, and where KMS fits in.
[00:27] Evan: Quick context - our current stack is multi-cloud (GCP primary, AWS DR), EKS, and we have Vault + GCP KMS. We want to avoid sending PHI to unknown places, so data residency and encryption are big.
[00:39] Priya: From ML side, latency matters for chat flows to clinicians, but cost matters too — we can't pay for ultra-low latency everywhere. We want a predictable SLA.
[00:48] Samir: Understood. Can I confirm: are you leaning hosted, dedicated, or private?
[00:53] Maya: Preference is dedicated reserved capacity if it meets our KMS + audit requirements. Private (VPC/on-prem) is a backup if dedicated can't provide the BYOK/HSM assurances.
[01:03] Lena: For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations on major clouds; explain: BYOK flows with KMS or HSM backing that we can integrate through our private key handshake - though there are subtle differences in on-prem HSMs.
[01:17] Evan: How does that work with GCP KMS? We already have key rotation policies and strict access controls via Vault.
[01:24] Lena: We can integrate with GCP KMS or AWS KMS; we don't hold plaintext keys in the control plane. Redwood can do envelope encryption where tokens are encrypted client-side, and the DEK (data encryption key) is wrapped by your KMS. Note: some older customers say "K-V cash" in logs — sorry that's a transcription slip — we mean KV cache for model context which we can control not to persist.
[01:47] Maya: Important: audit logs must include per-request metadata: user id, request id, model/version, route, timestamp, token counts, and whether content was persisted or cached. Also retention needs to be configurable to at least 7 years for some records.
[02:05] Lena: We emit structured audit logs; default fields include request_id, user_id (if passed), model, model_version, latency_ms, token_in, token_out, infra_node_id, and routing decision. Retention is configurable per account and per log type; however, longer retention often requires enterprise add-on.
[02:22] Tom: Cost question — how much does longer retention add? Our procurement needs an estimate.
[02:27] Samir: Longer log retention is an add-on priced based on volume and retention window. We'll send a very rough TCO sheet after this call.
[02:34] Maya: SOC2 and ISO — do you have attestations we can start reviewing? We have a compliance checklist.
[02:40] Samir: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 packages — I'll share the attestation excerpts and the control mappings. For Dedicated/Private there are slight differences in scope and evidence.
[02:52] Evan: On RBAC — can we map our internal AD groups to Redwood roles? We prefer SSO via SAML with SCIM for provisioning.
[02:59] Lena: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. We also support SCIM group sync and role templates to apply least privilege for developer, ops, and admin. For API keys we recommend short-lived tokens or a gateway pattern.
[03:16] Priya: Do API requests include user context in the trace so downstream logs for ML evaluation can attribute decisions?
[03:21] Lena: Yes, request-level metadata can include a user_id or session_id that you propagate; we log it as user_id in the event. There are some PII considerations — you can choose to hash or tokenise user identifiers before sending.
[03:34] Maya: About private deployments — how does the control plane work? We need to know if audit evidence is accessible during audits without exposing other customers.
[03:42] Samir: In Private deployments we provide a customer-dedicated control plane deployed into your VPC; all audit logs and metrics are stored in your account — you can ship logs to your SIEM or to a configured cloud bucket for retention. For Hosted/Dedicated, logs are multi-tenant in the control plane but logically segregated and accessible via per-tenant exports.
[04:02] Evan: Network-wise, does Redwood support VPC peering, PrivateLink, or VPN tunnels? We prefer PrivateLink if available.
[04:08] Lena: We offer VPC peering and PrivateLink equivalents in major clouds; for on-prem we have an edge gateway to broker traffic. We'll share network diagrams.
[04:18] Tom: Procurement note — what's the minimum commitment for Dedicated?
[04:22] Samir: Typically monthly reserved capacity or annual commit for predictability. We can provide a trial burst capacity for the pilot.
[04:28] Priya: For pilot benchmarks, we need: latency p95 under 250ms for typical clinical prompts (~256 tokens), consistent throughput for 100 concurrent sessions, and no leakage of PHI to logs except as we define.
[04:42] Lena: That's reasonable. For latency we can recommend model quantization and routing to lower-latency nodes. Also we can enable prefix caching for repeated prompts to clinicians. We'll propose a pilot config.
[04:57] Maya: Data residency — we need all inference for EU patients to remain in eu-west. Can you pin region routing?
[05:03] Lena: Yes, region pinning and routing policies are available. For Dedicated we can pin pools to regions. For Hosted we have region routing; for strict residency Private is the most straightforward.
[05:15] Evan: One technical concern: how do you handle KV cache in a shared environment? We need assurance that KV cache doesn't leak across tenants and that cached prompts aren't written to disk unencrypted.
[05:26] Lena: KV cache is kept in memory on the serving node and encrypted at rest if persisted; cross-tenant isolation is enforced at the runtime. We'll include runtime papers describing isolation primitives.
[05:38] Maya: On encryption: we need to see key rotation policies and proof that we don't hold plaintext master keys.
[05:44] Samir: We use envelope encryption — your KMS wraps our DEKs. We never persist plaintext master keys. Rotation is supported per your KMS schedule.
[05:52] Evan: HSM support? We use a Thales HSM on-prem and would prefer it for production keys.
[05:58] Lena: We can integrate with common HSMs via KMIP or cloud HSM APIs; for on-prem HSMs we'd normally run Private or a dedicated private connector to allow HSM-backed BYOK flows.
[06:12] Tom: Audit — if we run a SOC or ISO audit, can we get underlying logs and control evidence?
[06:17] Samir: Yes, we provide control evidence and log exports under NDA. For Hosted there is a standard pack; for Dedicated/Private we can provide more detailed operational logs.
[06:26] Maya: Any limitations on redaction? We may need redaction for PHI in logs before storage.
[06:31] Lena: You can configure pre-ingest processors to redact or tokenise fields. We also support outgoing webhook scrubbing and transformations.
[06:41] Priya: Slight tangent — are there guardrails for model updates/rollouts? We need the ability to pin model versions and run A/B rollouts.
[06:48] Samir: Yes, rollouts, canary, and automatic fallback are part of the platform. You can pin model versions per route, and we surface rollout metrics in the console.
[06:58] Evan: Can you stream logs to Splunk or BigQuery?
[07:02] Lena: Yes, we have connectors for Splunk, SIEMs, and cloud storage sinks to BigQuery / GCS.
[07:10] Tom: On pricing: send us a short rack of expected costs for pilot — latency tier, retention tier, and dedicated pool pricing.
[07:16] Samir: We'll send a pilot TCO with a few scenarios.
[07:22] Maya: Ok, I'm also going to ask: do you have any third-party pen-test or will you share penetration testing approach/attestation?
[07:29] Samir: We have third-party penetration test summaries and periodic scans. We'll include the latest report redacted for public details.
[07:37] Priya: One more — we need to know the default tokenization details for redaction: e.g., are there PII detectors out-of-the-box?
[07:44] Lena: There are built-in PII detectors and you can provide custom regex processors. Detection isn't perfect but it's part of the pilot to tune them.
[07:53] Maya: Decision criteria and timeline — we'll evaluate technical fit and compliance; procurement and legal will review pricing and contract. Target decision by 2026-12-10.
[08:03] Samir: Great. Proposed next: Lena will put together the pilot plan; Samir will send SOC2/ISO extracts and a TCO; we schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive for the infra team w/c network diagrams (suggested 2026-11-19).
[08:18] Evan: Sounds good. One note: our legal needs to see indemnity and data breach SLAs — can you share your standard contract redlines?
[08:26] Samir: We'll share a starter SOW and highlight breach notification timelines in the security pack.
[08:33] Tom: I'll coordinate procurement calendar and share PO timelines if the pilot hits the metrics.
[08:38] Maya: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the materials.
[08:42] (meeting wraps, small crosstalk)

Post-meeting recap (verbatim style):
- Pilot criteria: p95 latency < 250ms for 256-token prompts, 100 concurrent sessions, retention policy and log export configured.
- Compliance: Samir to send SOC2 Type II + ISO 27001 summaries + pen test summary.
- KMS: confirm BYOK flows with GCP KMS and HSM integration options; Evan to share Vault/KMS topology.
- SSO: SAML + SCIM for group mapping; RBAC templates to be demoed in deep-dive.

Notes about transcript quality and errors: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache), speaker overlaps, and informal filler words. Speakers sometimes used shorthand (PHI, KMS, HSM, KV).
